Custodian.definition: A person or institution that holds property belonging to another for safekeeping, without discretionary authority over its investment or disposition. Distinguished from a trustee, who holds legal title and owes fiduciary duties, and from an investment manager, who holds discretion over the property. A custodian's role is possession and safekeeping, not decision-making.
Custodian.source: Authored supplement - term postdates Black's 2nd ed. (1910), which has CUSTODY and CUSTODIA LEGIS but no CUSTODIAN headword

Settlor.definition: The person who creates a trust by transferring property to a trustee to hold for the benefit of a beneficiary. Also called grantor or trustor. Black's 2nd ed. treats this under SETTLEMENT.

Party In Interest.definition: Under ERISA, a person or entity with a defined relationship to an employee benefit plan - including a person providing services to the plan - whom a plan fiduciary might be inclined to favour at the expense of the plan's beneficiaries. Transactions between a plan and a party in interest are categorically barred by ERISA s.406(a) unless exempted. Being a party in interest does not make a person a fiduciary.

Beneficial Interest.definition: The right to enjoy the benefit of property whose legal title is held by another. Beneficial (equitable) ownership is distinct from legal ownership: a trustee may hold legal title while the entire beneficial interest rests with the beneficiary. Identifying who holds beneficial interest, and separately who holds control, is often more revealing of a relationship than who is named as owner.

Investment Manager.definition: A person to whom discretionary authority over the investment of property has been delegated. Under ERISA, exercising discretionary authority over plan assets makes a person a fiduciary of the plan regardless of title.
